ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number with 0 ≤ x. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer m such that m ≤ x. Since 0 is an integer and 0 ≤ x, the integer 0 is a candidate in this set. Therefore the greatest integer m ≤ x cannot be smaller than 0. Hence floor(x) ≥ 0.
